question: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) launched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2016.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment in August 2016 (for the financial year 2016-17). (प्रधानमंत्री रोजगार प्रोत्साहन योजना)

• Objective: to incentivise employers to create new jobs. Under the scheme the Government of India paid the employer's full contribution of 12% (8.33% EPS + 3.67% EPF) for new employees for a period of three years.

• It covered new employees earning less than ₹15,000 per month who were registered with the EPFO.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Registration under the scheme was open till 31 March 2019; beneficiaries continued to receive benefits for three years from the date of registration.

• Its successor scheme is the Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rozgar Yojana (ABRY), launched in October 2020.

NOTE

• Other employment/skilling schemes: PMKVY (2015, skill training), DDU-GKY (2014, rural youth), MGNREGA (2005, 100 days of wage employment), PM-SVANidhi (2020, street vendors).

question: The film based on which of the following novels by Amrita Pritam won the National Film Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pinjar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pinjar" (1950) is a celebrated Punjabi novel by Amrita Pritam set against the backdrop of the Partition of India (1947). Its heroine is Puro, a Hindu girl abducted by a Muslim man, Rashid.

• The 2003 Hindi film "Pinjar", directed by Chandraprakash Dwivedi and starring Urmila Matondkar and Manoj Bajpayee, won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film on National Integration. (पिंजर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Amrita Pritam (1919-2005) was the first prominent woman Punjabi poet/novelist. She was the first woman to receive the Sahitya Akademi Award (1956) for "Sunehade", won the Jnanpith Award (1981) for "Kagaz Te Canvas", and received the Padma Shri (1969) and Padma Vibhushan (2004).

• "Raseedi Ticket" (A Revenue Stamp) is her autobiography; "Nagmani" was the literary magazine she edited with Imroz.

• Her most famous poem is "Ajj Aakhaan Waris Shah Nu", written on the horrors of Partition.

NOTE

• Other Partition-themed literature: "Train to Pakistan" (Khushwant Singh), "Tamas" (Bhisham Sahni), "Toba Tek Singh" (Saadat Hasan Manto).

question: Which Indian Musician was awarded with the Bharat Ratna in 2001?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bismillah Khan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Bismillah Khan (1916-2006), the legendary shehnai maestro of Varanasi, was conferred the Bharat Ratna in 2001. (उस्ताद बिस्मिल्लाह खान — शहनाई)

• He was the third musician to receive the Bharat Ratna, after M. S. Subbulakshmi (1998) and Ravi Shankar (1999).

• He played the shehnai from the ramparts of the Red Fort on 15 August 1947, India's first Independence Day.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (Hindustani vocalist, Kirana gharana) received the Bharat Ratna in 2008.

• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma popularised the santoor; Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is a bansuri (flute) maestro. Both were awarded the Padma Vibhushan, not the Bharat Ratna.

NOTE

• The Bharat Ratna, instituted in 1954, is India's highest civilian award. Musicians honoured with it: M. S. Subbulakshmi, Ravi Shankar, Bismillah Khan, Bhimsen Joshi and Lata Mangeshkar (2001).

question: Who was the Prime Minster of India when the Fundamental Duties were first incorporated in the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indira Gandhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, when Indira Gandhi was the Prime Minister of India. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — 42वाँ संविधान संशोधन, 1976)

• They were incorporated as Part IV-A, Article 51A, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee (1976).

• Originally 10 duties were added; the 11th duty (a parent/guardian to provide education to a child between 6 and 14 years) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The idea of Fundamental Duties was borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

• The 42nd Amendment is called the "Mini-Constitution"; it also added the words Socialist, Secular and Integrity to the Preamble and inserted Part IV-A and Part XIV-A.

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by the courts.

NOTE

• The 86th Amendment (2002) also inserted Article 21A (Right to Education) and amended Article 45.

question:
Who said the following?

“Money is what money does.”
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prof. Walker.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous functional definition of money — "Money is what money does" — was given by the American economist Prof. Francis A. Walker. (धन वह है जो धन का कार्य करता है)

• The statement means that anything which performs the functions of money should be treated as money, irrespective of its physical form. It is therefore called the functional definition of money.

• The four classic functions of money are: a medium of exchange, a measure/unit of value, a store of value and a standard of deferred payment.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Prof. Seligman defined money as "one thing that possesses general acceptability".

• Prof. D. H. Robertson defined money as "anything which is widely accepted in payment for goods or in discharge of other kinds of business obligations".

• Prof. G. D. H. Cole described money as "purchasing power".

NOTE

• In India, currency notes are issued by the Reserve Bank of India (except the ₹1 note, issued by the Ministry of Finance) under the Minimum Reserve System followed since 1957.

question: Which of the following ports is located in Odisha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paradip Port.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Paradip Port is a major port on the east coast of India, located in the Jagatsinghpur district of Odisha, at the confluence of the Mahanadi river and the Bay of Bengal. (पारादीप बंदरगाह — ओडिशा)

• It is India's first major port built and managed by an Indian entity after Independence and was commissioned in 1966. It is a deep-water port handling large volumes of iron ore, coal and petroleum.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Haldia Port — West Bengal (part of Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, Kolkata).

• Kandla Port (Deendayal Port) — Gujarat, on the Gulf of Kachchh; a tidal port.

• Tuticorin Port (V. O. Chidambaranar Port) — Tamil Nadu.

NOTE

• Major ports on the east coast: Kolkata/Haldia, Paradip, Visakhapatnam, Kamarajar (Ennore), Chennai, V. O. Chidambaranar. On the west coast: Deendayal (Kandla), Mumbai, JNPT, Mormugao, New Mangalore, Cochin.

question: Rohini Bhate, Pandit Munnalal Shukla, Kumudini Lakhia and Uma Sharma are famous exponents of which of the following classical dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rohini Bhate, Pandit Munnalal Shukla, Kumudini Lakhia and Uma Sharma are all celebrated exponents of Kathak, the classical dance of North India (especially Uttar Pradesh). (कथक)

• The word Kathak comes from "katha" (story) — the "kathakars" were storytellers who narrated epics through dance.

• Its distinctive features are intricate footwork (tatkar), rapid spins (chakkars) and expressive abhinaya; it is the only classical dance form with strong Persian/Mughal influence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kathak gharanas: Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh.

• Other famous Kathak dancers: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Shambhu Maharaj, Lachhu Maharaj, Damayanti Joshi, Shovana Narayan.

• Rohini Bhate was the first Kathak exponent from Maharashtra to receive the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award; Kumudini Lakhia founded the Kadamb dance institute in Ahmedabad.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: The forces exerted on a body during a short period are known as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Impulse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Impulse is the effect of a large force acting on a body for a very short interval of time. It is measured as the product of force and the time for which it acts. (आवेग)

◦ Impulse (J) = Force × Time = F × Δt

• By Newton's second law, impulse equals the change in momentum of the body: J = Δp = m·v − m·u (the impulse-momentum theorem).

• Its SI unit is the newton-second (N·s), which is equivalent to kg·m/s. It is a vector quantity.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pressure = force per unit area (P = F/A), SI unit pascal (Pa).

• Surface tension is the property by which the free surface of a liquid behaves like a stretched membrane; SI unit N/m.

• Tensile stress is the internal restoring force per unit area in a body being stretched; SI unit N/m² (pascal).

NOTE

• Everyday applications of impulse: a cricketer draws his hands back while catching a ball, and vehicles have airbags and crumple zones — both increase the time of impact and hence reduce the force for the same change in momentum.

question: India played the final of ODI Cricket World Cup 2011 against which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sri Lanka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India defeated Sri Lanka in the final of the ICC Cricket World Cup 2011, played at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, on 2 April 2011. India won by 6 wickets, chasing 275. (2011 विश्व कप — भारत विजेता)

• Mahendra Singh Dhoni captained the side and was Man of the Match (91 off 79 balls); Gautam Gambhir scored 97. Yuvraj Singh was named Player of the Tournament.

• It was India's second World Cup title (after 1983 under Kapil Dev) and the first time a host nation won the World Cup.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The 2011 World Cup was co-hosted by India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.

• India also won the 2013 and 2025 ICC Champions Trophy, the 2007 T20 World Cup and the 2024 T20 World Cup.

NOTE

• ODI World Cup winners: 1975, 1979 & 1999 West Indies/Australia (1975 & 1979 WI; 1999 Australia), 1983 India, 1987 Australia, 1992 Pakistan, 1996 Sri Lanka, 2003 & 2007 Australia, 2011 India, 2015 Australia, 2019 England, 2023 Australia.

question: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance style belongs to ________________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form of the state of Kerala. The name literally means "the dance of the enchantress" (Mohini — the female avatar of Lord Vishnu; attam — dance). (मोहिनीअट्टम — केरल)

• It is a solo dance traditionally performed by women, marked by graceful, swaying (lasya) movements, a white-and-gold kasavu sari costume and a bun of hair worn on the left side.

• The songs are usually in Manipravalam (a mixture of Sanskrit and Malayalam) and are set to Carnatic music; the chief accompanying instruments are the maddalam, idakka, mridangam and veena.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Famous exponents: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma (called the "mother of Mohiniyattam"), Sunanda Nair, Bharati Shivaji, Kanak Rele.

• The poet Vallathol Narayana Menon, founder of the Kerala Kalamandalam (1930), played a key role in reviving Mohiniyattam.

NOTE

• Kerala's other art forms: Kathakali (classical dance-drama), Koodiyattam (UNESCO-listed Sanskrit theatre), Theyyam, Ottamthullal and the martial art Kalaripayattu.

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Indian political party system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Single party system.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India has a multi-party system, not a single-party system. Any number of parties may be formed and contest elections; hence "single party system" is not a feature of the Indian party system. (भारत में बहुदलीय व्यवस्था है)

• India's diversity of religion, language, caste and region, together with universal adult franchise, has produced a large number of national and State (regional) parties.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Genuine features of the Indian party system include: a multi-party system, one-party dominance in the early decades (the "Congress system"), lack of an effective/strong opposition at times, factionalism, defections and splits, personality cults, and the presence of strong regional parties and coalition politics.

• The Anti-Defection Law was introduced by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1985, adding the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution.

NOTE

• Recognition of parties is done by the Election Commission of India under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. A single-party system exists in countries such as China and North Korea.

question: Which of the following was the first Satyagraha Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi in British India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Champaran Satyagraha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 (Bihar) was Mahatma Gandhi's first Satyagraha in India. (चंपारण सत्याग्रह, 1917)

• It was launched on the invitation of the local peasant leader Raj Kumar Shukla against the oppressive "tinkathia system", under which indigo planters forced peasants to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land.

• The agitation succeeded: the Champaran Agrarian Act, 1918 abolished the tinkathia system, and part of the illegal exactions was refunded.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kheda Satyagraha (1918, Gujarat) — a no-revenue campaign by peasants hit by crop failure; Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel assisted Gandhi.

• Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918) — Gandhi's first hunger strike, on behalf of mill workers.

• Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919) — Gandhi's first all-India mass agitation, against the Rowlatt Act.

• Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) — led by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, who earned the title "Sardar".

NOTE

• Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915 (celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas). His political mentor was Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

question: Dr. Teejan Bai, who was awarded by Padma Vibhushan (2019) is a renowned Indian folk singer and performer from the state of ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhattisgarh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Teejan Bai is a legendary exponent of Pandavani, the traditional folk ballad form of Chhattisgarh in which episodes from the Mahabharata are narrated in song with a tambura in hand. (तीजन बाई — पंडवानी, छत्तीसगढ़)

• She was born in 1956 at Ganiyari village, Durg district, Chhattisgarh, and was the first woman to perform Pandavani, which had earlier been a male preserve.

• Awards: Padma Shri (1988), Padma Bhushan (2003), Padma Vibhushan (2019) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1995).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pandavani has two styles — Vedamati (the singer sits) and Kapalik (the singer stands and acts); Teejan Bai performs in the Kapalik style.

• Other folk forms of Chhattisgarh: Panthi, Raut Nacha, Karma, Saila and the folk theatre Nacha.

NOTE

• Folk traditions elsewhere: Bihu (Assam), Ghoomar and Kalbelia (Rajasthan), Nati (Himachal Pradesh), Bihu/Ojapali (Assam), Lavani (Maharashtra), Bhangra/Giddha (Punjab).

question: The fundamental vocabulary of __________ dance constitutes mock combat techniques, stylised gaits of birds and animals and movements modelled on the chores of village housewives and mostly performed by male dancers in Eastern India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chhau.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhau is a semi-classical masked dance of Eastern India, whose vocabulary is built on mock combat techniques (from martial arts), stylised gaits of birds and animals and movements modelled on village household chores. It is performed mainly by male dancers. (छऊ नृत्य)

• It has three styles named after their places of origin:

◦ Seraikella Chhau — Jharkhand (masks used)

◦ Purulia Chhau — West Bengal (large, elaborate masks)

◦ Mayurbhanj Chhau — Odisha (performed without masks)

• Chhau was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• It is traditionally performed during the Chaitra Parva spring festival; themes are drawn from the Ramayana, Mahabharata and local folklore.

• Manipuri (Manipur) is known for its gentle Raas Leela; Kathakali (Kerala) is a masked/painted-face dance-drama; Sattriya (Assam) was created by the saint Srimanta Sankardeva.

NOTE

• Indian entries on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list include Koodiyattam, Vedic chanting, Ramlila, Chhau, Kalbelia, Buddhist chanting of Ladakh, Sankirtana of Manipur, Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja of Kolkata and Garba of Gujarat.

question: The Red Fort is located in:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Red Fort (Lal Qila) is located in Delhi, on the banks of the Yamuna. It was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan between 1638 and 1648 when he shifted his capital from Agra to Shahjahanabad. (लाल क़िला — दिल्ली)

• Its architect was Ustad Ahmad Lahauri, and it is built chiefly of red sandstone — hence the name.

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007. The Prime Minister hoists the national flag here and addresses the nation from its ramparts every 15 August.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Important structures inside: Diwan-i-Aam (hall of public audience), Diwan-i-Khas (hall of private audience, where the Peacock Throne was kept), Rang Mahal, Moti Masjid, Hira Mahal and the Lahori and Delhi Gates.

• The Kohinoor diamond once adorned the Peacock Throne, which was carried away by Nadir Shah in 1739.

NOTE

• Other Mughal monuments: Taj Mahal and Agra Fort (Agra), Fatehpur Sikri and Buland Darwaza (Akbar), Humayun's Tomb (Delhi), Jama Masjid (Delhi, Shah Jahan).

question: The Goa government launched a new scheme in November 2022 for which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dev Darshan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In November 2022, the Government of Goa launched the "Dev Darshan Yojana" (also called the Dev Darshan scheme). (देव दर्शन योजना — गोवा)

• Under the scheme, free/subsidised bus transport is provided so that people — particularly students, senior citizens and members of village institutions — can visit temples, churches and other places of worship and pilgrimage within Goa.

• The aim is to promote religious tourism, cultural awareness and communal harmony in the State.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Chief Minister of Goa at the time of the launch was Dr. Pramod Sawant.

• Goa is India's smallest State by area; its capital is Panaji and it was liberated from Portuguese rule on 19 December 1961 (Operation Vijay) and became a full State on 30 May 1987.

NOTE

• Other pilgrimage-related government schemes: PRASHAD (Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Augmentation Drive) and Swadesh Darshan of the Union Ministry of Tourism.

question: Ruturaj Gaikwad became the first batsman in List-A cricket to hit how many sixes in an over?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ruturaj Gaikwad, playing for Maharashtra against Uttar Pradesh in the Vijay Hazare Trophy 2022 quarter-final (February 2022, Ahmedabad), hit 7 sixes in a single over — a world record in List-A cricket. (रुतुराज गायकवाड़ — एक ओवर में 7 छक्के)

• The over was bowled by the UP left-arm spinner Shiva Singh and included a no-ball, which is why eight deliveries were bowled and seven of them went for six — 43 runs came off the over.

• Gaikwad scored an unbeaten 220 off 159 balls in that innings.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Batsmen who have hit 6 sixes in an over: Garfield Sobers (1968, first-class), Ravi Shastri (1985, first-class), Herschelle Gibbs (2007 World Cup, ODI), Yuvraj Singh (2007 T20 World Cup, off Stuart Broad), Kieron Pollard (2021 T20I) and Nicholas Pooran / Thisara Perera in other formats.

• The Vijay Hazare Trophy is India's premier domestic 50-over (List-A) tournament.

NOTE

• Ruturaj Gaikwad plays for Chennai Super Kings in the IPL and won the Orange Cap in IPL 2021.

question: The author of ‘Malgudi Days’ is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is RK Narayan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Malgudi Days" (1943) is a celebrated collection of short stories by R. K. Narayan (Rasipuram Krishnaswami Iyer Narayanaswami, 1906-2001). (आर. के. नारायण)

• The stories are set in the fictional South Indian town of Malgudi, which appears throughout his works. The book was adapted into a famous Doordarshan television series (1986) directed by Shankar Nag.

• R. K. Narayan received the Sahitya Akademi Award (1958) for "The Guide", the Padma Bhushan (1964) and the Padma Vibhushan (2000); he was also nominated to the Rajya Sabha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other works by R. K. Narayan: "Swami and Friends", "The Bachelor of Arts", "The English Teacher", "The Guide", "The Man-Eater of Malgudi", "The Vendor of Sweets".

• Rabindranath Tagore — "Gitanjali" (Nobel Prize, 1913), "Gora", "Ghare Baire".

• Vikram Seth — "A Suitable Boy", "The Golden Gate".

• Chetan Bhagat — "Five Point Someone", "2 States", "The 3 Mistakes of My Life".

NOTE

• The "Big Three" of early Indian English fiction are R. K. Narayan, Mulk Raj Anand ("Untouchable", "Coolie") and Raja Rao ("Kanthapura").

question: Camels are found in which type of forests in India from the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The thorn forest and scrubs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Camels are found in the tropical thorn forests and scrubs of India — the vegetation of semi-arid and arid regions such as Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, where rainfall is less than 70 cm. (कँटीले वन एवं झाड़ियाँ)

• Typical plants are acacia (babool), khair, kikar, palms, euphorbias, cacti and khejri, with long roots and thick/waxy or spiny leaves to conserve water.

• Typical animals: camel, wild ass, horses, rats, mice, rabbits, fox, wolf, tiger, lion.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Tropical evergreen forests — rainfall above 200 cm (Western Ghats, north-east, Andaman & Nicobar); animals: elephant, monkey, lemur, deer.

• Mangrove/tidal forests — deltas of the Ganga, Mahanadi, Godavari and Krishna; the Sundarbans are famous for the Royal Bengal Tiger and the sundari tree.

• Montane forests — Himalayan slopes; animals: Kashmiri stag, snow leopard, yak, ibex, red panda.

NOTE

• The camel is the State animal of Rajasthan, and the Khejri (Prosopis cineraria) is its State tree. The Bikaner camel research centre is the National Research Centre on Camel.

question: Under whom among the following British Governor-Generals was the new policy of ‘paramountcy’ initiated in British India by the East India Company?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Hastings.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The policy of "Paramountcy" was initiated under Lord Hastings (Governor-General, 1813-1823). (सर्वोच्चता की नीति — लॉर्ड हेस्टिंग्स)

• Under this policy the East India Company claimed that its authority was 'paramount' or supreme over all Indian States; therefore it could annex or threaten to annex any Indian kingdom to protect its own interests.

• The doctrine was justified as necessary for the "protection" of Indian states, and it laid the ground for later expansionist measures.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Lord Wellesley (1798-1805) introduced the Subsidiary Alliance — Hyderabad was the first state to accept it (1798).

• Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856) introduced the Doctrine of Lapse, under which Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur and Awadh were annexed.

• Lord Cornwallis (1786-1793) introduced the Permanent Settlement (1793) in Bengal and is called the "father of the Indian Civil Service".

• Lord Amherst (1823-1828) fought the First Anglo-Burmese War (1824-26), ended by the Treaty of Yandabo (1826).

NOTE

• Under Lord Hastings the Anglo-Nepalese War (1814-16) ended with the Treaty of Sugauli, and the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817-18) destroyed the Maratha confederacy.

question: Paryushana Parva is a festival of which of the following communities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Paryushana Parva is the most important annual festival of the Jain community, observed during the monsoon (Bhadrapada, August-September). (पर्युषण पर्व — जैन धर्म)

• It lasts eight days for the Svetambara sect and ten days for the Digambara sect (where it is called Das Lakshana Parva). Devotees observe fasting, prayer, scriptural reading and repentance.

• It ends with "Michhami Dukkadam" (Kshamavani/Samvatsari) — the day of universal forgiveness, when Jains ask pardon of all living beings for any harm caused.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other Jain festivals: Mahavir Jayanti and Diwali (marking the nirvana of Mahavira).

• Jainism was founded on the teachings of 24 Tirthankaras; the first was Rishabhanatha (Adinatha) and the 24th was Vardhamana Mahavira (599-527 BCE), born at Kundagrama (Vaishali).

• The three jewels (Triratna) of Jainism: Right Faith, Right Knowledge and Right Conduct. Its central principle is Ahimsa (non-violence).

NOTE

• The two main Jain sects — Svetambara (white-clad) and Digambara (sky-clad) — arose after the famine in Magadha during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya.

question: Who coined the word ‘cell’ in the 1600s, from the Latin word ‘cellula’, meaning ‘small room’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Robert Hooke.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The English scientist Robert Hooke coined the term "cell" in 1665 while examining a thin slice of cork under his self-designed compound microscope. (रॉबर्ट हुक — कोशिका)

• The box-like compartments he saw reminded him of the small rooms (cells) in a monastery, so he named them after the Latin "cellula" meaning "small room".

• He published his observations in his book "Micrographia" (1665). What he actually saw were the dead cell walls of cork tissue.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Anton van Leeuwenhoek (1674) first observed living cells (bacteria, protozoa) and is called the "Father of Microbiology".

• Robert Brown (1831) discovered the nucleus; Purkinje (1839) coined the term protoplasm.

• The Cell Theory was proposed by M. J. Schleiden (1838) and Theodor Schwann (1839), and completed by Rudolf Virchow (1855) — "Omnis cellula-e cellula" (all cells arise from pre-existing cells).

• Louis Pasteur — germ theory and pasteurisation; Lynn Margulis — the endosymbiotic theory of mitochondria and chloroplasts.

NOTE

• The cell is the structural and functional unit of life. The largest cell is the ostrich egg and the longest cell is the nerve cell; the smallest cell is that of Mycoplasma (PPLO).

question: Which of the following is a feature of Micro Finance Institutions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Financial service to disadvantaged people.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) provide small-value financial services — micro credit, savings, insurance and remittances — to low-income, disadvantaged and unbanked people who cannot access formal banking. (सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थाएँ)

• Loans are usually collateral-free, of small size, and given largely to women and to Self Help Groups (SHGs) and Joint Liability Groups (JLGs) for income-generating activities.

• The aim is financial inclusion and poverty alleviation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• MFIs registered as NBFC-MFIs are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India; the RBI issued a revised regulatory framework for microfinance loans in March 2022 (defining a microfinance loan as a collateral-free loan to a household with annual income up to ₹3 lakh).

• NABARD launched the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme in 1992, the world's largest microfinance programme.

• Bandhan Bank and Ujjivan, Equitas, Suryoday (Small Finance Banks) evolved from microfinance institutions.

NOTE

• Prof. Muhammad Yunus of Bangladesh, founder of the Grameen Bank, is called the "Father of Microfinance"; he won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.

question: Which of the following States became the overall champions in both the men’s and women’s categories in the 2023 Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Odisha emerged as the overall champion in both the men's and women's categories of the Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav 2023 (the National Tribal Sports Meet). (जनजातीय खेल महोत्सव 2023 — ओडिशा)

• The event was organised by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs in collaboration with the Sports Authority of India (SAI) and was held at Deendayal Upadhyaya Sports Complex, New Delhi (June 2023).

• Tribal athletes from across the country competed in disciplines such as athletics, archery, football, volleyball, kabaddi and tug-of-war.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The festival aims to give a national platform to tribal sporting talent and to identify athletes for higher-level training.

• Odisha is also known for its strong support to sports — it sponsors the Indian men's and women's hockey teams and hosted the FIH Men's Hockey World Cup in 2018 and 2023.

NOTE

• Related observances: Janjatiya Gaurav Divas is celebrated on 15 November, the birth anniversary of the tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda. The Khelo India Youth Games is the flagship national grassroots sports programme.

question: The mohororvicic (Moho) discontinuity separates?
option_3: Earth's crust and the inner core
solution_text:
The correct answer is Earth's crust and the mantle.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Mohorovičić discontinuity, popularly called the "Moho", is the boundary that separates the Earth's crust from the mantle. (मोहो असंबद्धता — भूपर्पटी और मैंटल के बीच)

• It was discovered in 1909 by the Croatian seismologist Andrija Mohorovičić, who noticed that seismic waves suddenly increase in velocity at this depth.

• Its depth is about 5-10 km beneath the oceanic crust and about 30-70 km beneath the continents (deepest under high mountain ranges).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other discontinuities inside the Earth:

◦ Conrad discontinuity — between the upper (SIAL) and lower (SIMA) continental crust.

◦ Repetti discontinuity — between the upper and lower mantle.

◦ Gutenberg discontinuity — between the mantle and the outer core (at about 2,900 km).

◦ Lehmann discontinuity — between the outer core and the inner core.

NOTE

• S-waves (secondary/transverse waves) cannot pass through liquids, which is how scientists proved that the outer core is in a liquid state. P-waves travel through solids, liquids and gases.
